title: Tip-Adapter: Training-Free Adaption of CLIP for Few-Shot Classification
key_mechanism: Training-free key-value cache built directly from the few-shot support set (image features as keys, one-hot labels as values); test-time query is classified by CLIP zero-shot logits fused with a similarity-weighted vote over the cache. Tip-Adapter-F unfreezes the cache keys as a linear layer and fine-tunes them with SGD for a further boost.
evaluation_datasets: 11 image classification datasets (ImageNet, Caltech101, etc.), 1/2/4/8/16-shot
notes: Foundational training-free cache-adaptation reference; the fusion of a frozen backbone score with a similarity-weighted cache vote is structurally the closest published analogue to the lead's L0/L1 fused-score design, but built for closed-set few-shot classification, not anomaly detection or streaming operator feedback. No OA fulltext found (closed access); verified via OpenAlex/CrossRef metadata (title, authors, venue, DOI) and cross-checked with the official GitHub, not a fetched abstract or full text.

title: Efficient Test-Time Adaptation of Vision-Language Models (TDA)
key_mechanism: Training-free Dynamic Adapter (TDA) keeps two key-value caches per class populated online at test time: a low-entropy 'positive' pseudo-label cache (bounded priority queue per class, admits a new sample only if it is more confident than the current worst entry) and a 'negative' cache that stores samples with entropy in a chosen band and a multi-hot label mask over the classes the sample is NOT confidently assigned to, used to subtract support for wrong classes. Both caches are combined with the frozen CLIP zero-shot logit at inference; no backward pass or weight update is ever performed.
evaluation_datasets: ImageNet distribution-shift benchmarks (ImageNet-A/V2/R/Sketch) and 10 cross-domain classification datasets, single-pass streaming test order
notes: Closest published structural analogue to the lead's normal/fault dual-cache design (positive cache = normal-cache role, negative cache = a mechanism for excluding false hypotheses). Key differences from the thesis design: (1) caches are populated from the model's OWN pseudo-labels/entropy, never from a human-confirmed feedback signal; (2) there is no delayed/asynchronous feedback, no 'quarantine' state, and no adaptation-harm accounting; (3) task is closed-set multi-class image classification under distribution shift, not open-ended anomaly detection with an unbounded space of unseen fault types. Read in full (12 pages) via arXiv PDF.

title: Dual Memory Networks: A Versatile Adaptation Approach for Vision-Language Models (DMN)
key_mechanism: Maintains a 'static' memory built from few-shot labeled support samples plus a 'dynamic' memory that accumulates unlabeled test-time samples (with pseudo-labels), each queried via an attention-like weighted-similarity readout instead of a simple kNN vote; unifies zero-shot, few-shot and test-time-adaptation settings in one dual-memory model, with an optional lightly-tuned projection for a 'DMN-F' variant.
evaluation_datasets: Same 11-dataset few-shot benchmark plus OOD/cross-domain benchmarks used by Tip-Adapter/TDA
notes: Extends the cache idea with a learned attention-style readout and explicitly separates a static (curated) memory from a dynamic (test-time-accumulated) one, structurally close to a normal-cache/adaptation-cache split, but again driven by pseudo-labels, not confirmed operator feedback, and for image classification. Read in full via arXiv PDF (16 pages, key sections reviewed).

title: Dual Prototype Evolving for Test-Time Generalization of Vision-Language Models (DPE)
key_mechanism: Evolves two sets of prototypes online — textual and visual — that are progressively updated (not just appended-to, like a cache) from accumulated multi-modal test-time knowledge, with a learned residual to align text and visual prototype spaces at test time; positioned as an improvement over TDA/Tip-Adapter-style static caches by allowing the stored representations themselves to drift with incoming data.
evaluation_datasets: Same OOD/cross-domain CLIP TTA benchmark suite as TDA/DMN
notes: Directly relevant to the 'benign aging/new-normal absorption' half of the thesis problem: DPE's prototypes are allowed to evolve (drift) rather than just accumulate, which is the vision-language analogue of absorbing benign drift into the cache. Still self-supervised (no human feedback loop) and for image classification. Read in full via arXiv PDF.

title: BoostAdapter: Improving Vision-Language Test-Time Adaptation via Regional Bootstrapping
key_mechanism: Boosts a training-free cache-based TTA baseline (in the Tip-Adapter/TDA family) by bootstrapping additional pseudo-samples from regional crops/augmentations of each test image before admitting entries to the cache, improving cache quality without weight updates.
evaluation_datasets: Same CLIP OOD/cross-domain TTA benchmarks
notes: Confirms the cache-TTA line is still active through 2024 with variants that improve cache population quality; no time-series or anomaly-detection transfer. Verified via OpenAlex abstract.

title: WinCLIP: Zero-/Few-Shot Anomaly Classification and Segmentation
key_mechanism: Zero-/few-normal-shot visual anomaly classification+segmentation with CLIP: compositional prompt ensembles score window-level image patches against normal/anomalous text prompts; the few-normal-shot variant (WinCLIP+) stores CLIP features of the handful of provided normal reference images and compares test-patch features to them via a multi-scale reference similarity, functioning as a small normal-only memory (no anomaly/fault cache, no feedback loop).
evaluation_datasets: MVTec-AD, VisA
notes: Confirmed via OpenAlex abstract. Normal-only reference memory (few images), not a growing dual cache and not time-series.

title: PromptAD: Learning Prompts with only Normal Samples for Few-Shot Anomaly Detection
key_mechanism: Learns normal/abnormal prompt pairs from only normal few-shot samples by manufacturing pseudo-anomaly prompts (semantic concatenation) so a one-class prompt-learning objective becomes tractable; no explicit non-parametric key-value cache — the 'memory' is compressed into learned prompt vectors that ARE tuned (this is closer to the thesis's L2 adapter tier than L0 cache tier).
evaluation_datasets: MVTec-AD, VisA
notes: Confirmed via OpenAlex abstract. Relevant contrast case: shows that for one-class few-shot visual AD, prompt-tuning (a lightweight parametric update) rather than a static cache was needed to make conventional many-class prompt learning work — indirect evidence for when cache-only underperforms.

title: AnomalyCLIP: Object-agnostic Prompt Learning for Zero-shot Anomaly Detection
key_mechanism: Learns a single object-agnostic text prompt pair (generic 'normal'/'damaged object' semantics rather than per-class prompts) so a CLIP-based zero-shot anomaly detector trained once on one set of object classes generalizes to unseen object classes without any per-target-class memory or cache at all.
evaluation_datasets: 17 industrial/medical AD benchmarks (MVTec-AD, VisA, and others), cross-domain zero-shot transfer
notes: Confirmed via OpenAlex abstract. Zero-shot generalist AD without any target-specific cache; relevant as an example of a 'no-adaptation' generalist AD baseline the thesis's frozen-backbone-only condition should be compared against.

title: Toward Generalist Anomaly Detection via In-Context Residual Learning with Few-Shot Sample Prompts (InCTRL)
key_mechanism: Trains one Generalist AD (GAD) model across many source datasets that is then given, at inference on a NEW target dataset, only a handful of in-context few-shot normal example images (no gradient update on the target); the model computes a holistic residual between the query image and its in-context normal exemplars plus a residual against a fixed normal-image memory bank built from the same few-shot set, combining a class-agnostic learned residual scorer with a small non-parametric normal-image memory read at test time.
evaluation_datasets: 9 real-world AD benchmarks spanning industrial defect and medical images, cross-dataset GAD protocol
notes: The closest published match to the thesis's 'frozen universal backbone + few-shot commissioning via memory, no weight update' framing outside of time series: pretrain once, freeze, then at deployment read a small non-parametric memory of few-shot NORMAL exemplars. It has no fault/anomaly cache (no confirmed-anomaly memory), no feedback loop, no drift-absorption mechanism, and is for static images, not sequential/temporal machine signals. Read in full via full-text fetch.

title: MuSc: Zero-Shot Industrial Anomaly Classification and Segmentation with Mutual Scoring of the Unlabeled Images
key_mechanism: Zero-shot (no normal reference at all): treats the unlabeled test batch itself as a mutual-scoring pool, exploiting that normal patches recur frequently across the unlabeled test set while anomalous patches do not, to assign anomaly scores without any stored memory from training or a support set.
evaluation_datasets: MVTec-AD, VisA
notes: Confirmed via OpenAlex abstract. Interesting negative case: achieves zero-shot AD via mutual comparison within a test batch rather than any persistent cache, showing an alternative to memory-based adaptation entirely; not directly transferable to a streaming single-machine deployment where a 'batch of the same machine' assumption doesn't hold the same way.

title: Catching Both Gray and Black Swans: Open-set Supervised Anomaly Detection (DRA)
authors_short: Ding, Pang, Shen, Van den Hengel
key_mechanism: Disentangled Representation learning for open-set supervised Anomaly detection (DRA): decomposes an image's anomaly score into four learned components -- seen-anomaly-class similarity, pseudo-anomaly (synthetically generated) similarity, a residual/discrepancy term, and a normal-class term -- each with its own small memory/branch, trained jointly so the model generalizes from a handful of SEEN anomaly classes (e.g. one fault type) to detect anomaly types never seen during training (the 'black swans'), while still scoring the seen types well ('gray swans').
evaluation_datasets: MVTec-AD, and hierarchical/composite open-set splits built from AITEX, SDD, ELPV, Optical, Mastcam datasets
notes: Directly relevant as the vision analogue of the thesis's 'new, previously unseen anomaly types after deployment' requirement: DRA is trained (weights move) to generalize from few seen fault classes to unseen ones, which is the parametric (L2-style) counterpart to what the thesis wants a training-free fault cache to achieve. It is a TRAINING-time method with fixed weights at test time (not an online growing cache, no feedback loop, not time series). Read in full via arXiv PDF (16 pages).

title: Anomaly Heterogeneity Learning for Open-set Supervised Anomaly Detection
key_mechanism: Extends DRA-style open-set supervised AD by explicitly modeling heterogeneity among the seen anomaly classes (rather than treating them as one pooled class) to better separate genuinely novel unseen-anomaly patterns from variance within known fault types.
evaluation_datasets: MVTec-AD-based open-set splits and additional industrial defect datasets
notes: Confirmed via OpenAlex abstract. Shows the DRA line continuing to 2023-2024; relevant to the thesis's need to distinguish new fault-type variance from known-fault variance in a fault cache.

title: Distribution Prototype Diffusion Learning for Open-set Supervised Anomaly Detection
key_mechanism: Models the distribution of normal-sample prototypes with a diffusion process (rather than a single unimodal Gaussian prior) to sharpen the decision boundary in open-set supervised AD, addressing the same seen-to-unseen-anomaly generalization problem as DRA with a more expressive normal-prototype model.
evaluation_datasets: Open-set AD image benchmarks (per abstract)
notes: Confirmed via OpenAlex abstract only (author list not independently verified beyond the OpenAlex record). Shows the open-set-AD line is active into 2025 but still image-domain.

title: Mixture Prototype Flow Matching for Open-Set Supervised Anomaly Detection
key_mechanism: Replaces the unimodal-Gaussian normal-prototype assumption of prior open-set supervised AD methods with a multi-modal mixture-prototype model learned via flow matching, aiming for sharper decision boundaries when normal data is itself multi-modal.
evaluation_datasets: Open-set AD image benchmarks (per abstract)
notes: Confirmed via OpenAlex abstract only. Latest (2026) entry in the open-set-AD line found at this search depth; still image-domain, still a trained (weights-move) model, not a growing test-time cache and not time series.

title: DeepLog: Anomaly Detection and Diagnosis from System Logs through Deep Learning
key_mechanism: LSTM-based log-sequence anomaly detector with an explicit online-update workflow: when an operator marks a flagged sequence as a false positive, DeepLog incrementally retrains/updates the underlying LSTM on the newly confirmed-normal sequence rather than discarding the feedback, so the model's notion of normal execution paths evolves with confirmed operator input.
evaluation_datasets: HDFS and OpenStack system logs
notes: Verified via CrossRef metadata (title/authors/venue/DOI); full text not fetched this session. Established precedent (2017) for a feedback-triggered weight UPDATE upon confirmed false positive, but it retrains the parametric model directly rather than routing feedback into a non-parametric cache, and predates the cache-adapter literature entirely.

title: Incorporating Expert Feedback into Active Anomaly Discovery (AAD)
key_mechanism: Active Anomaly Discovery: an ensemble tree-based anomaly detector re-ranks its anomaly scores after each analyst label (confirmed anomaly / confirmed normal) by treating the re-weighting of ensemble members as an online linear-model update, so a small number of expert labels progressively pushes true anomalies to the top of the ranked queue.
evaluation_datasets: Standard outlier-detection benchmark suite (~20 UCI-derived datasets)
notes: Verified via CrossRef/OpenAlex metadata (no OA full text located; closed-access IEEE proceedings). Foundational active/feedback-driven AD reference: shows the alternative to caching is re-weighting the SCORING FUNCTION itself online from sparse labels, i.e., a lightweight parametric (L1-style) update rather than a non-parametric cache.

title: Feedback-Guided Anomaly Discovery via Online Optimization
key_mechanism: Formalizes updating an anomaly ranking from analyst feedback as an online convex optimization problem, giving a simpler and more efficient feedback-incorporation rule than the AAD line; demonstrated on tree-based detectors plus a cybersecurity red-team-detection case study.
evaluation_datasets: Outlier benchmark suite plus real system audit-log red-team-attack data
notes: Abstract confirmed via Unpaywall/OpenAlex metadata. Same lineage as AAD: online re-weighting of the parametric scoring function from feedback, not a cache; explicitly targets reducing analyst effort by moving false positives down / true positives up the ranking, directly analogous to the thesis's dismissed-false-alarm and confirmed-fault feedback signals.

title: An Interactive Dive into Time-Series Anomaly Detection
key_mechanism: System demonstration letting a user interactively explore/inspect univariate time-series anomaly-detection results and compare detector outputs; primarily a visualization/exploration tool rather than a feedback-driven learning or adaptation mechanism.
evaluation_datasets: Standard univariate TSAD benchmark collections (per venue norms)
notes: Verified via CrossRef metadata only; full text not fetched. Confirms 'interactive TSAD' work published in 2024 is largely about visualization/exploration of detector output, not closed-loop feedback that updates the detector's cache or weights -- supporting the gap that closed-loop operator-feedback adaptation for TSAD is under-addressed.

title: Deep Anomaly Detection with Deviation Networks (DevNet)
key_mechanism: End-to-end neural 'deviation learning': directly optimizes anomaly scores (rather than learning a representation and scoring post hoc) to be statistically deviant from a reference normal score distribution, using only a handful (multiple to dozens) of labeled anomalies plus a prior, making it data-efficient under a small label budget.
evaluation_datasets: ~40 tabular outlier-detection benchmark datasets with synthetically limited anomaly labels
notes: Confirmed via OpenAlex/Unpaywall abstract. Same family of thinking as the thesis's 'confirmed fault -> fault cache' but for a trained parametric scoring head rather than a non-parametric memory; a natural L2 baseline to compare against a fault cache under matched few-label budgets, though evaluated on static tabular data, not sequential machine signals.

title: Toward Deep Supervised Anomaly Detection: Reinforcement Learning from Partially Labeled Anomaly Data
authors_short: Pang, van den Hengel, Shen, Cao
code_url: https://github.com/GuansongPang/ARM-Net (repo name varies; check paper for released code link)
key_mechanism: Frames anomaly detection under partial anomaly labels as a reinforcement-learning problem where an agent sequentially decides which unlabeled instances to score as anomalous, using the sparse labeled anomalies as a partial reward signal, to better exploit unlabeled data alongside the few confirmed anomalies.
evaluation_datasets: Multiple tabular AD benchmarks
notes: Verified via arXiv API listing (title/id/date only; abstract not independently fetched this session). Another parametric (weights-move) approach to sparse anomaly-label incorporation, useful as an L2-tier comparison point.
